resale_co.how_to_apply: The Township's Construction Office page tells sellers that the Fire District Office handles resale inspections; no separate township resale certificate is described. See the fire certificate section.

evidence.quote: Selling Your House? The Fire District Office handles inspections for resale. You will need to have your house inspected before you go to settlement;
Selling your house? You will need to have your house inspected before you go to settlement,
Bill Lunemann Construction Official Director of Construction Department

resale_co.notes: The Township does not say in so many words that no CO is needed, but its Construction Office page answers 'Selling Your House?' by sending sellers only to the Fire District Office for the resale (smoke/CO) inspection. The Construction Office also posts the generic state UCC 'Application for Certificate' (form F270, rev. 6/2003, marked 'Cost: $150.00', with boxes for CO, CCO, lead clearance and temporary CO); it is for construction permits and change of use, not described as a resale requirement. The Township code (ecode360 DE1570) could not be opened. Status would change to required if the code shows a resale CCO ordinance.

requirements: Older homes need 10-year sealed battery smoke alarms (or AC powered alarms) on each level and outside sleeping areas

Homes built with hardwired, battery backup, interconnected alarms (for example Summer Hill, Forest Hill, Waters Edge, The Grande, the Orchard) must keep them on each level and in each bedroom, and they must be less than 10 years old
Carbon monoxide detectors must be less than 5 years old (check the manufacture or replace-by date) and installed outside each sleeping area
All smoke and CO detectors must be UL listed
House number: Arabic numerals, contrasting color, at least 3 inches tall, at least 30 inches above ground, visible from the street (Township Code Chapter 95)
The current form (February 2025) does not list a portable fire extinguisher

authorities.name: Delran Township Fire District No. 1, Bureau of Fire Prevention (Local Enforcing Agency)
authorities.lead_time: Apply more than 10 business days (excluding holidays) before the change of occupant for the lowest fee. Payment is due before the inspection.

fees.label: Request received more than 10 business days before closing
fees.quote: Requests for inspection received more than 10 business days excluding holidays prior to the change of occupant: $45.00

fees.label: Request received 4 to 10 business days before closing
fees.quote: Requests for inspection received four to 10 business days excluding holidays prior to the change of occupant: $90.00

fees.label: Request received fewer than 4 business days before closing
fees.quote: Requests for inspection received fewer than four business days excluding holidays prior to the change of occupant: $161.00

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Inspection (Smoke Detector and CO Detector) and email it to LEA@delranfire.org or drop it off at the Fire District office in the Municipal Building, 900 S. Chester Avenue, Delran. Pay before the inspection by check payable to Delran Fire District #1 or online (list the inspection address as the invoice number).

evidence.quote: N.J. State Fire Code N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3 requires the inspection of One & Two Family Dwellings and R-2 Occupancies for smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors before it is sold or leased.
MAKE CHECK PAYABLE TO DELRAN FIRE DISTRICT #1 OR PAY ONLINE ON OUR WEBSITE
Please contact our office anytime at (856) 461-5474 or by email at LEA@delranfire.org
When making the payment please list the address of the inspection as the invoice number.
The Bureau of Fire Prevention and the Local Enforcement Agency are also part of Delran Township Fire District #1. These agencies are headed up by Fire Official Joseph Cunningham, Jr.
